To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the reduced proliferative response of cells cultured in serum on fibrillar collagen is a direct result, at least in part, of the reduced responsiveness of these cells to platelet‐derived mitogen.

the reduced proliferative response of fibroblast cells to serum and PDGF when cultured on reconstitued fibrillar collagen, as compared to plastic substrates, is due to the direct influence of the extracellualr matrix on cell responsiveness to these growth factors.

the reduced proliferation of adult human skin cells cultured on reconstitute fibrillar collagen is not due to differences in the ability of the cells to attach to the substratum, but is due to the reduced responsiveness of the cells to PDGF when cultured on collagen as compared to plastic.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of the microenvironment on cellular proliferation.
the interaction between fibroblasts and their extracellular environment.
the interaction between the extracellular matrix and the cells that synthesize it and with the effect that the matrix has on the growth and differentiation of the cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reduced proliferation of human skin fibrolasts cultured on collagen fibrillar gel is due to the reduced responsiveness of the cells to PDGF.

cells cultured on collagen gals have reduced responsiveness to PDGF and that this reduced response to PDGF is largely responsible for the reduction in the proliferative activity of cells on collagen gels.
the reduced proliferative capacity of fibroblastic cells cultured on collagen gells, when compared to plastic, is a consequence of the reduced responsiveness of the cells to PDGF.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the extracellular matrix can have a profound effect on cell proliferation.
the extracellular matrix is an important regulator of the proliferative response to PDGF.

the reduced proliferative capacity of cells cultured on collagen gals is not due to a reduction in PDGF binding to the cells, but rather to an alteration in the intracellular response of the cell to this growth factor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the extracellular matrix is a dynamic component of the cell microenvironment that is capable of regulating the proliferative activity of cells in response to growth factors and hormones.
the extracellular matrix can influence the proliferative response to growth factors.

the extracellular matrix can have a direct influence on the proliferative activity of cells, independent of its role in cell attachment and independent of its role as a reservoir of soluble mitogenic mediators.
